result.summary: Isolates all legacy wallet loading and migration logic into a dedicated `wallet/legacy` subdirectory and a `wallet::legacy_migration` namespace. It introduces a `LegacyWallet` subclass of `CWallet` to hold legacy-only routines, extracts `LegacyDataSPKM` into its own file, and separates legacy loading from normal descriptor wallet loading.
result.problem: Although Bitcoin Core no longer supports directly loading legacy wallets, legacy wallet loading and migration logic remains co-mingled with descriptor wallet code in `CWallet` and wallet database loaders. This coupling clutters the active descriptor codebase and risks accidental calls to legacy routines.
evidence: Author states: "Now that we no longer support loading legacy wallets, there is no reason to keep any of the legacy wallet loading and migration code in the main wallet objects. Having this co-mingling of never-to-be-changed legacy wallet code and new descriptor wallet code makes it difficult to implement new things into the wallet." (PR description)
result.scope_notes: Large structural refactor across 24 files (+2611/-2334 lines) with several move-only commits, file renames, and a new `LegacyWallet` subclass, incorporating commits from #34909 and #36823.
result.card: This PR isolates all legacy wallet migration and loading logic into a dedicated `wallet/legacy` directory under a `wallet::legacy_migration` namespace, moving legacy-only methods into a new `LegacyWallet` subclass of `CWallet`. It eliminates co-mingled legacy code from the main descriptor wallet codebase now that direct legacy wallet loading is unsupported, preventing accidental cross-usage. Builds upon #34909 and depends on #36823.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in the prompt, so exact changes outside commit messages cannot be verified.

risk.why: Mistakes in wallet loading or record parsing during migration could corrupt wallet databases or cause migrations from legacy wallets to fail.
